revocation.title: Lock and Destroy
revocation.hint: Lock erases every keyslot of the disk and reboots the device; it can be restored with the escrowed header and recovery key. Destroy also deletes the escrow, so the data cannot be recovered; a second administrator must approve it.
revocation.reasonHint: Shown to the administrators and kept with the request.

lock.label: Lock device
lock.title: Lock the device
lock.confirm: The device {hostname} erases every keyslot of its disk and reboots with its next check-in. Nobody can unlock it until an administrator restores it with the escrowed header and recovery key.

destroy.label: Destroy device
destroy.title: Destroy the device
destroy.confirm: The escrowed header and recovery key of {hostname} are deleted and the device erases every keyslot of its disk. Its data cannot be recovered. A second administrator must approve this request before anything happens.

requested.lock: The lock was requested. The device locks itself with its next check-in.
requested.destroy: The destroy was requested. It waits for the approval of a second administrator on the Revocations page.

profiles.rootEquivalentEffective: The combined commands hand out root: {commands}. This is reported as full rights.
profiles.fullConfirm: Create {name} with full sudo rights? Everyone it is assigned to becomes root on their devices.
profiles.toFullConfirm: Give {name} full sudo rights? Everyone it is assigned to becomes root on their devices.

profiles.deleteConfirm: Delete {name}? Profiles that are still assigned cannot be deleted.

sessionActions.terminate: End the user's sessions (unsaved work is lost)

loginSettings.sessionActionHint: What devices do with the open sessions of a locked user.

approve.title: Approve the destroy

dms.title: Dead man's switch
dms.warning: If Paddock is unreachable for longer than this period, every device with the switch enabled locks itself.
dms.enabled: Turn on the dead man's switch
dms.periodHint: Days of uptime without reaching Paddock after which a device locks itself.
dms.periodInvalid: Enter a whole number of days from {min} to {max}.
dms.shortPeriod: Periods below {days} days lock devices that are merely offline for a while, for example during a vacation.
dms.warnDaysHint: Comma-separated, for example 3, 1: the user sees a warning that many days before the device locks itself.
dms.warnDaysInvalid: Enter up to five whole numbers of days, each at least 1 and shorter than the period.
dms.saved: The settings were saved. Devices receive them with their next check-in.

confirm.title: Turn on the dead man's switch
confirm.message: Every device of the organization locks itself after {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} of uptime without reaching Paddock, also when Paddock itself is down. A locked device must be restored with its escrowed header and recovery key.
confirm.label: Turn on
